06.steps:
1.Config interface as WAN zone
2.Choose "PPPoE" in "IP Assignment"
3.Check "Unnumbered interface:" checkbox, and choose "Create new unnumber interface" in the drop-down list
06.title: GUI: The unnumbered interface can be created via "Create new unnumber interface" option in WAN PPPoE setting page
06.result: in step3, a new page pop up and can create success

12.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface, config X2 IP in PPPoE server pool
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2, check X1 status
12.title: Func: When the unnumbered interface IP match the PPPoE server pool address, verify the PPPoE unnumbered interface can get connected, the connected IP should be the same with the unnumbered interface.
12.result: in step2, X1 IP is the same with X2 IP

15.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2, make sure X1 get connected
3.Check NAT polices
15.title: Func: Verify after the PPPoE unnumbered interface get connected, DUT will auto add two NAT policies (between the PPPoE interface and the unnumbered interface)
15.result:
in step3, two polices added:
Policy #1. From unnumbered interface subnet to any, translated src as original.
Policy #2. From any to the PPPoE unnumbered interface subnet, translated dst as original.

16.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface, PC1 connect to X2
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2, PC2 connect to X1, make sure X1 get connected
3.PC1 ping PC2, visit PC2 IP via HTTPS and download file via FTP
4.PC2 ping PC1, visit PC1 IP via HTTPS and download file via FTP
5.Check capture packet
16.title: Func: Verify after the PPPoE unnumbered interface get connected, the traffic (ping/FTP/HTTPS) between unnumbered interface host and WAN host should be successful, the data flow should not do NAT
16.result:
in step3&4, all traffic go through success
in step5, the data flow do not NAT

20.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface, enable Management(ping/https/snmp/ssh)
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2
3.Enable SNMP in System->SNMP page
4.PC connect to X2, PC ping X2 IP and visit X2 IP using Explorer and secureCRT, using MIB to get info
20.title: Management (ping/https/snmp/ssh) from LAN/DMZ PC (connected to the unnumbered interface) to the unnumbered interface should be fine
20.result: in step4, all function work well

25.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2
3.Click "Connect" button
4.Click "Disconnect" button
25.title: Disconnect/reconnect PPPoE unnumbered interface from GUI,check if work fine
25.result:
in step3, PPPoE can get IP
in step4, PPPoE disconnect

29.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2
3.After X1 get IP, change X1 to another mode(Specify IP address/Obtiain IP address)
29.title: If PPPoE unnumbered interface change from unnumbered mode to another mode(Specify Ip address/Obtiain Ip address) , it should can reconnect successfully.

32.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2
3.After X1 get the same IP with X2, change X2 IP, check log monitor and packet
32.title: If change ip of unnumbered interface, PPPoE unnumbered should reconnect again and PPPoE ip should be the same with the unnumbered interface.
32.result: in step3, X1 IP become the same with the new X2 IP, log and packet show a new PPPoE negotiation

41.steps:
1.Config X2 as LAN unnumbered interface, PC1 connect X2; config X3 as LAN normal interface, PC2 connect X3
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2, make sure X1 get connected
3.Allow ACL WAN->LAN
4.Create inbound NAT policy:
Any Orignal X1 IP PC1 IP Any Orignal WAN interface Any
5.WAN PC ping X1 IP, capture packet
6.Change inbound NAT policy:
Any Orignal X1 IP PC2 IP Any Orignal WAN interface Any
7.Repeat step5
Notice: Change the priority of user-defined NAT policies in step4&6, they should be higher than the auto-added NATs in case 15
41.title: WAN to LAN NAT test, create inbound NAT policy to translate DST IP from PPPoE unnumbered interface IP to LAN host IP
41.result: in step5&7, the packet show the data flow destination IP was translated

43.steps:
1.Config X2 as unnumbered interface
2.Config WAN X1 as PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumber to X2
3.Shutdown/no shut X1, check X1 status
43.title: Link down/up test for unnumbered PPPoE interface: after link up, it will reconnect and function is back
43.result: in step2&3, X1 can get IP

51.steps:
1.Config LAN unnumbered interface X3, add a DHCP server scope for X3
2.PC connect X3 and can get IP
3.Disconnect PPPoE unnumbered interface, PC release/renew
4.Reconnect PPPoE unnumbered interface, PC release/renew
51.title: Add dhcp server for the unnumbered interface, disconnect and reconnect the PPPoE unnumbered interface, veirfy DHCP server still work
51.result: in step3&4, PC can get IP

71.steps:

2.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interface
3.Ping traffic from LAN PC to Internet website
4.Restart the FW

71.result: in step4, PC ping traffic success again

72.steps:

2.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface
3.After WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface connected, download TSR
72.title: Verify in TSR all the information for PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumbered interface are correct
72.result: All info about PPPoE unnumbered interface and unnumbered interface are correct in TSR

73.steps:
1.Config several LAN unnumbered interfaces
2.Config several WAN PPPoE unnumbered interfaces, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interfaces
3.After WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface connected, export prefs
4.Change some unnumbered interface settings and import prefs

76.steps:
1.Config LAN unnumbered interface with PC connected, add available DHCP server scope for this interface
2.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interface
3.PC visit Internet website using Ping traffic, capture packet and check Ping traffic
4.Enable HA, check PC's traffic

76.result: in step4, traffic is passing through and no stop

78.steps:
1.Enable HA
2.Config LAN unnumbered interface with PC connected, add available DHCP server scope for this interface
3.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interface
4.PC visit Internet website using Ping traffic, capture packet and check Ping traffic

6.Login active DUT, check PPPoE unnumbered interface IP and PC's traffic
78.title: [HA]Verify PPPoE can reconnect with the same IP and traffic is successful after failover due to reboot
78.result: in step6, PPPoE unnumbered interface IP is the same and traffic go pass success

84.steps:
1.Enable HA
2.Config LAN unnumbered interface with PC connected, add available DHCP server scope for this interface
3.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interface
4.PC visit Internet website using Ping traffic, capture packet and check Ping traffic
5.Change PPPoE unnumbered interface settings, such as PPPoE username/password, inactivity and reconnect options, MTU, etc.
6.Check PPPoE unnumbered interface setting in idle DUT
84.title: [HA]Verify after PPPoE unnumbered interface settings changed in the active FW, the settings will be synced to the idle one, like PPPoE username/password, inactivity and reconnect options, MTU, etc.
84.result: in step6, PPPoE settings are syn success

85.steps:
1.Enable HA
2.Config LAN unnumbered interface with PC connected, add available DHCP server scope for this interface
3.Config WAN PPPoE unnumbered interface, unnumber to LAN unnumbered interface, enable Management(ping/https/snmp/ssh)
4.WAN host ping PPPoE unnumbered interface IP and visit X1 IP using Explorer and secureCRT, using MIB to get info
5.Click "Force Active/Standy failover" button in High Availability-Advanced page
6.Repeat step4
85.title: [HA]Management via PPPoE unnumbered interface after failover, including ping/https/snmp/ssh.
85.result: in step4&6, all function work well
